findings.highlight: The monthly managerial meeting will be held at the end of this week, and I'm thinking of showing up then.
findings.evidenceJa: 今週末に月一の上司面談だから、そこで申し出てみようと思う
findings.explanation: This is Haruki's monthly interview with his supervisor, and he plans to ask there about returning to work. Todokanai TL turns it into a generic managerial meeting he may attend, omitting the actual proposal that makes Setsuna anxious.
findings.japanese:
『今週末に月一の上司面談だから、
そこで申し出てみようと思う』
findings.todokanai: "The monthly managerial meeting will be held at the end of this week, and I'm thinking of showing up then."

findings.highlight: the days are just as cheerfully warm as I remember.
findings.evidenceJa: 日中は思い出したように汗ばむ陽気になったりして、これからやってくる蒸し暑さに思いを馳せる頃
findings.explanation: The days now occasionally remember to grow warm enough to make people sweat, prompting thoughts of the muggy heat still to come. Todokanai TL invents remembered cheerful warmth and drops the forward-looking seasonal image.
findings.japanese:
まだ朝夕は涼しいけれど、
日中は思い出したように汗ばむ陽気になったりして、
これからやってくる蒸し暑さに思いを馳せる頃。
findings.todokanai: The mornings and evenings are still chilly, but the days are just as cheerfully warm as I remember.

findings.highlight: Haruki-kun sent me a text.
findings.evidenceJa: 春希くんが、メールを再開した
findings.explanation: Haruki has resumed emailing: the point is a recovered channel of communication after a period of silence, not the arrival of one isolated text. The reduction breaks the milestone developed in the surrounding paragraphs.
findings.japanese: 春希くんが、メールを再開した。
findings.todokanai: Haruki-kun sent me a text.

findings.highlight: He didn't even charge his cell phone until very recently. Even now, he never calls me nor answers any of my calls.
findings.evidenceJa: しばらく、携帯の電源すら入れられなかったけれど。今もまだ、電話はかけられないし、出られないけれど
findings.explanation: Haruki was unable even to turn the phone on, and still cannot place or answer calls at all. Todokanai TL changes powering it on into charging it and narrows a general incapacity into behavior specifically toward Setsuna.
findings.japanese:
しばらく、携帯の電源すら入れられなかったけれど。
今もまだ、電話はかけられないし、出られないけれど。
findings.todokanai: He didn't even charge his cell phone until very recently. Even now, he never calls me nor answers any of my calls.

findings.highlight: Then on top of that, I maintain a bit more distance
findings.evidenceJa: …彼を怯えさせないように、息苦しさを感じさせないように、ほんの少しだけ距離を置いて
findings.explanation: Setsuna first tells herself the small distance is to keep Haruki dry, then corrects herself: it is really so she will not frighten or suffocate him. Todokanai TL makes this a second, additional increase in distance and destroys the revealing self-correction.
findings.japanese:
…彼を怯えさせないように、
息苦しさを感じさせないように、
ほんの少しだけ距離を置いて。
findings.todokanai: Then on top of that, I maintain a bit more distance, so that I don't scare him… so that I don't make him feel suffocated.

findings.highlight: a postcard with everyone's names on it.
findings.evidenceJa: 寄せ書きだってくれたじゃない、みんな
findings.explanation: His colleagues gave him a group-written message board, described on the next line as a shikishi displayed beside his bed. A postcard bearing names is the wrong object and loses the personal messages gathered for his recovery.
findings.japanese:
「だからぁ、春希くんだって必要とされてるよ。
寄せ書きだってくれたじゃない、みんな」
findings.todokanai: "I keep telling you, you're needed as well. They even sent you a postcard with everyone's names on it."

findings.highlight: a piece of colored paper, sent by the editorial staff of Kaiousha.
findings.evidenceJa: 開桜グラフ編集部の人たちが贈ってくれた色紙
findings.explanation: The gift is a shikishi message board from the Kaiou Graph editorial department. Todokanai TL reads 色紙 literally as colored paper and substitutes a company-like 'Kaiousha' for the named publication, breaking both the physical scene and institutional continuity.
findings.japanese:
彼のベッドの脇には、
開桜グラフ編集部の人たちが贈ってくれた
色紙が飾られている。
findings.todokanai: Beside his bed lies a piece of colored paper, sent by the editorial staff of Kaiousha.

findings.highlight: far from what he intended
findings.evidenceJa: 多分、彼が意図したものとはちょっとだけ違ってて
findings.explanation: Setsuna says the pain differs only a little from what Haruki intended, a fine distinction before she explains why his betrayal proves feelings can endure. 'Far from' reverses that degree and makes the connection much looser than the Japanese.
findings.japanese:
けれどその痛みは、
多分、彼が意図したものとはちょっとだけ違ってて。
findings.todokanai: But that inflicted pain is far from what he intended with those words.

findings.highlight: when I had to sit beside you for five years as you kept thinking about Kazusa.
findings.evidenceJa: 五年もかずさを忘れなかったあなたが側にいるから、信じられてしまうんだよ
findings.explanation: Setsuna can believe in unfading love because the man beside her now failed to forget Kazusa for five years. Todokanai TL instead says Setsuna sat beside him throughout those five years and 'had to' believe, changing both the timeline and her painful logic.
findings.japanese:
五年もかずさを忘れなかったあなたが側にいるから、
信じられてしまうんだよ…
findings.todokanai: I had no choice but to believe it, when I had to sit beside you for five years as you kept thinking about Kazusa.

findings.highlight: I'm doing this because I want to…
findings.evidenceJa: だから、それはわたしのワガママで
findings.explanation: Setsuna explicitly calls remaining beside Haruki her own selfishness. Todokanai TL reduces the morally charged ワガママ to neutral personal desire, cleaning away her characteristic self-indictment.
findings.japanese: 「だから、それはわたしのワガママで…」
findings.todokanai: "I told you, I'm doing this because I want to…"

findings.highlight: once every two weeks or so.
findings.evidenceJa: 十日に一度くらい陥る
findings.explanation: The severe crash occurs about once every ten days, not once every two weeks. This is a direct numerical error in Setsuna's account of Haruki's condition.
findings.japanese:
昨日の彼は、わたしが側にいるだけで参ってしまうほどの、
十日に一度くらい陥る、どん底の状態だったから。
findings.todokanai: Yesterday, he was in such a terrible state that just having me around was enough to ruin him, something that only happens once every two weeks or so.

findings.highlight: The sound of the rain and the darkness of the sky seeped into the tepidness of his room, robbing him of any courage or joy he had left.
findings.evidenceJa: 雨の音と、空の暗さと、生温い空気にあてられて、元気も、勇気も奪われてしまっていたから
findings.explanation: The rain, dark sky, and lukewarm air acted on Haruki and robbed him of vigor and courage. Todokanai TL makes rain and darkness seep into 'the tepidness of his room,' a causal relationship absent from the source, and changes vigor into joy.
findings.japanese:
雨の音と、空の暗さと、生温い空気にあてられて、
元気も、勇気も奪われてしまっていたから。
findings.todokanai: The sound of the rain and the darkness of the sky seeped into the tepidness of his room, robbing him of any courage or joy he had left.

findings.highlight: no matter how much I tried to console him, encourage him, or embrace him.
findings.evidenceJa: 慰めても、励ましても、優しくしても
findings.explanation: Setsuna says that consoling, encouraging, or treating him gently has never restored his strength. Todokanai TL invents embracing him, immediately before the text explains that on such days she cannot safely embrace him.
findings.japanese:
そんな日は、慰めても、励ましても、優しくしても、
春希くんが力を取り戻すことは、経験上ない。
findings.todokanai: On days like that, I never managed to restore Haruki-kun's strength, no matter how much I tried to console him, encourage him, or embrace him.

findings.highlight: I'm always caught in a struggle between myself and my low blood pressure, which keeps trying to hold me tied down to bed.
findings.evidenceJa: 低血圧と戦いながら、ゆっくりと体を起こす
findings.explanation: The sentence culminates in Setsuna slowly sitting herself up while fighting her low blood pressure. Todokanai TL translates the subordinate struggle but omits the main physical action.
findings.japanese:
休みの日の朝になると、
いつもわたしをベッドに縛り付けようとする
低血圧と戦いながら、ゆっくりと体を起こす。
findings.todokanai: Every weekend morning, I'm always caught in a struggle between myself and my low blood pressure, which keeps trying to hold me tied down to bed.

findings.highlight: only told me out of convenience.
findings.evidenceJa: 彼女と、ついでにわたしにしか話さない
findings.explanation: Setsuna downgrades herself to an afterthought: he told Kazusa, and incidentally her. 'Out of convenience' invents a utilitarian motive and changes the precise form of Setsuna's self-abasement.
findings.japanese:
ううん、彼女と、ついでにわたしにしか話さない、
彼の、切り捨てた過去のこと。
findings.todokanai: No, he told her first and only told me out of convenience. About the past he had cast away.

findings.highlight: he lost sight of his family when he was younger.
findings.evidenceJa: 子供の頃の行き違いがもとで捻れてしまっているだけかもしれない
findings.explanation: Setsuna's father suggests a childhood misunderstanding may simply have twisted the relationship. Todokanai TL replaces the misunderstanding with Haruki 'losing sight' of his family, an event not stated in the Japanese.
findings.japanese:
「単に、子供の頃の行き違いがもとで
捻れてしまっているだけかもしれない。
一度、母親の真意を確かめる必要があるんじゃないか？」
findings.todokanai: "He might simply be in a bad way because he lost sight of his family when he was younger. Shouldn't we at least ask his mother what she thinks?"

findings.highlight: We can just set things straight if there was simply a misunderstanding between them.
findings.evidenceJa: けれど、もし彼の言う通り、根が深いのであれば、もっと色々考えていかなければならない
findings.explanation: The father contrasts an easily resolved misunderstanding with the possibility that the roots are as deep as Haruki says, in which case the families must consider much more. Todokanai TL deletes the complete second half, leaving the next question without its antecedent.
findings.japanese:
「単なる誤解だったら解けばいい。
けれど、もし彼の言う通り、根が深いのであれば、
もっと色々考えていかなければならない」
findings.todokanai: "We can just set things straight if there was simply a misunderstanding between them.

findings.highlight: the way you're handling it isn't doing him any good.
findings.evidenceJa: だからって、今のままでは何も進まないじゃないか
findings.explanation: Her father says that even so, nothing will move forward if things remain as they are. Todokanai TL turns an impersonal stalemate into an accusation that Setsuna's handling is ineffective, adding blame not present in the line.
findings.japanese: 「だからって、今のままでは何も進まないじゃないか」
findings.todokanai: "But the way you're handling it isn't doing him any good."

findings.highlight: I hit the nail on the head.
findings.evidenceJa: その目論見はみごとに的中した
findings.explanation: Setsuna's scheme to draw her mother into the argument appeared to work exactly as planned. 'Hit the nail on the head' normally means making a correct diagnosis or statement, not successfully executing a scheme, so the English assigns the success to the wrong kind of act.
findings.japanese: そして、その目論見はみごとに的中した。
findings.todokanai: And I hit the nail on the head.

findings.highlight: we weren't on speaking terms with his family
findings.evidenceJa: 家族同士が知り合いでない方が後々いいんじゃないかと
findings.explanation: Setsuna's mother says it may be better later if the two families never become acquainted. Todokanai TL's 'weren't on speaking terms' implies an existing acquaintance followed by estrangement, changing the preventive argument she is making.
findings.japanese:
「そういう場合は、家族同士が知り合いでない方が
後々いいんじゃないかと…」
findings.todokanai: "Then perhaps it'd be better if… we weren't on speaking terms with his family…"

findings.highlight: She simply had her own reason.
findings.evidenceJa: ただ、たまたま思惑が一致しただけ
findings.explanation: The revelation is that mother and daughter happened to want the same immediate outcome for entirely different reasons. Todokanai TL notes only that her mother had a reason, omitting the accidental alignment that explains the apparent support.
findings.japanese: ただ、たまたま思惑が一致しただけ。
findings.todokanai: She simply had her own reason.

findings.highlight: I thought about going back…
findings.evidenceJa: 仕方なく踵を返して玄関に戻る
findings.explanation: Setsuna actually turns on her heel and returns to the entryway, where she notices she is wearing slip-ons. Todokanai TL changes the completed movement into merely thinking about returning.
findings.japanese:
仕方なく踵を返して玄関に戻る。
…と、その踵に履いていたものもただの突っかけだった。
findings.todokanai: Deeming it a lost cause, I thought about going back… Only then realizing that I had left in my slippers.

findings.highlight: She's starting to wonder whether something bad happened between you and Kitahara-san.
findings.evidenceJa: それも、婚約とか言い出した頃からさ
findings.explanation: Takahiro adds that their mother suspects the trouble began around the time Setsuna started talking about engagement. Todokanai TL drops that complete timing clause and leaves the quotation open.
findings.japanese:
「姉ちゃんと北原さん、
なんかトラブルがあったんじゃないかって。
それも、婚約とか言い出した頃からさ」
findings.todokanai: "She's starting to wonder whether something bad happened between you and Kitahara-san.

findings.highlight: Until just recently, you both treated him like family
findings.evidenceJa: 二人とも、今まで彼のこと、ずっと家族みたいにしてくれてたじゃない
findings.explanation: Setsuna protests that they have treated Haruki like family all along up to the present crisis. 'Until just recently' says that treatment had already stopped, contradicting the continuity asserted by 今まで and ずっと.
findings.japanese:
「二人とも、今まで彼のこと、
ずっと家族みたいにしてくれてたじゃない！」
findings.todokanai: "Both of you! Until just recently, you both treated him like family, didn't you!?"

findings.highlight: Why do you have to grasp at straws like that!?
findings.evidenceJa: どうしてそういう揚げ足ばっかり取るのよ
findings.explanation: Setsuna accuses Takahiro of constantly seizing on verbal slips and inconsistencies. 'Grasp at straws' means making a desperate weak attempt, not pedantically catching somebody's wording, so the English accusation is the wrong one.
findings.japanese: 「っ！　どうしてそういう揚げ足ばっかり取るのよ！」
findings.todokanai: "…! Why do you have to grasp at straws like that!?"

findings.highlight: This is an important time for me right now.
findings.evidenceJa: 今が大事な時期なんだよ
findings.explanation: The critical period is Haruki's recovery and the need to support him carefully, not a special period for Setsuna personally. Todokanai TL inserts 'for me,' shifting the center of the argument away from the patient she is discussing.
findings.japanese:
「今が大事な時期なんだよ。
お父さんもお母さんも、
そのことが全然わかってないんだよ」
findings.todokanai: "This is an important time for me right now. Mom and dad don't understand that at all."

findings.highlight: Mom has started to entertain the thought of us breaking up.
findings.evidenceJa: 孝宏は、彼の誠実を疑うようになり
findings.explanation: The three-part family inventory ends with Takahiro beginning to doubt Haruki's sincerity. Todokanai TL omits that entire third clause, breaking the parallel and deleting the brother's distinct concern.
findings.japanese:
お父さんは、彼を家族から家族候補に格下げし。
お母さんは、わたしたちが別れる可能性を否定しなくなり。
孝宏は、彼の誠実を疑うようになり。
findings.todokanai: Dad has demoted him from "family member" to "potential family member." Mom has started to entertain the thought of us breaking up.

findings.highlight: I've got nothing to do with this
findings.evidenceJa: 俺は、部外者だから
findings.explanation: Takahiro modestly calls himself an outsider to the couple's relationship, which limits his right to pronounce on it. Todokanai TL says he has nothing to do with the situation at all, disowning an involvement his conduct and family position plainly retain.
findings.japanese:
「俺は、部外者だから
そうそうえらそうなことは言えないけどさ…」
findings.todokanai: "I've got nothing to do with this, so I can't act like I know everything, but…"
